correctness.rationale: The exact final claim is a finite complete classification, not a partial enumeration. Height four means four vertices in a longest chain; in a rooted poset the sole depth-3 point is the root. Nonroot depth-1 points immediately cover distinct subsets of the 3 maxima of cardinality at least 2, yielding at most one for each of four sets ab/ac/bc/abc and hence Q_T. Nonroot depth-2 point covers an antichain of at least 2 points containing at least one depth-1 vertex; conversely any such antichain defines a unique depth-2 point without duplicate cover sets. The selected nonempty family U cannot be the singleton of all minimal points of Q_T, which otherwise leaves the root with only one cover. All other U give root at least 2 covers, and its cover set includes a depth-2 point, preventing coincidence. Induction on depth reconstructs every source poset uniquely. With labelled maxima, sums of (2^|A(T)|-2) give 16718; S3 relabeling exhausts all isomorphisms because cover sets force every lower vertex, with fixed counts identity 16718, transpositions 1070 each, 3-cycles 68 each, yielding (16718+3*1070+2*68)/6=3344. The source correctly invokes the published equivalence of finite regular Esakia duals and cover-set regular posets (Grilletti–Quadrellaro, Theorem 4.7), and 3 maxima give 8 double-negation-fixed elements (Corollary 3.5). An independently written exact Python program, not executing the repository verifier, enumerated ALL 16718 normal-form choices; reconstructed closure and cover edges for each, tested least root, 3 maxima, unique nonmaximal successor sets of size >=2, height 4, canonical S3 orbits and fixed counts, matching 3344, and size range 7..22. The independent enumeration corroborates the finite census; the conceptual exhaustive-normal-form proof establishes completeness.

originality.rationale: Grilletti–Quadrellaro (arXiv:2303.11246, Algebra Universalis 85:5) provides Theorem 4.7, the necessary-and-sufficient finite regular-cover criterion, and Corollary 3.5 relating Boolean fixed elements to maxima. Its Section 5 gives special infinite families with three maxima, while Section 7 expressly asks for classification of finite regular posets by depth/maxima; the journal text examined does not provide this complete height-four three-maxima 3344-orbit census or its S3-equivariant antichain normal form. Fresh queries through Resultary, published SCOPE records, and public literature for the exact pair of restrictions, alternative rooted-frame terminology, and integers 3344/16718 found no covering published count; nonmatching hits are not novelty proof. The result is therefore best-of-knowledge original as the exact bounded complete classification, while crediting the crucial prior duality and membership theorem.

value.rationale: The original primary work specifically asks for a classification of finite regular Esakia posets by combinatorial dimensions, including depth and number of maximal elements. Three maxima constitute an 8-element regular Boolean core; height four is a natural first nontrivial case with interacting two-level antichain choices below that core. The reversible, S3-equivariant normal form is mathematically useful independently of the integer: it parametrizes representatives and bounds size (7 through 22 vertices). The complete 3344-class result resolves that meaningful bounded problem and constrains finite regularly generated, subdirectly irreducible Heyting-algebra examples. The result does not claim distinct logics, full algebra sizes, a classification for other depths or arbitrary numbers of maxima, and does not rely on novelty or the verifier alone to establish value.
